editorial:
Imagine coming home after a long day and having to face a tragedy that never ends. You meet a couple who are stuck in a nightmare, caring for their daughter who is basically a shell of a person after a bad accident. Instead of just crying, they use a really dark kind of humor to get through it. They actually take turns speaking for her, making up funny or mean things she might say if she could talk. It is a weird mix of being heartbreaking and strangely funny at the same time, making you wonder how any parents could actually cope with this kind of pain.

The acting is the best part here because it feels so real and raw. You will feel the tension in the room as they fight and then laugh. The pacing is slow, which helps you feel how long and boring their days have become. If you like stories that look at the messy side of life, you should definitely check this out. You can find it for rent on Apple TV if you want a quick watch, but adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move for fans of old-school drama.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a sad and honest note. After all the jokes and pretending, the parents cannot escape the reality that their daughter will never get better. They realize that their dark humor was just a shield to keep them from breaking down. The story wraps up by showing that while they love her, they are completely exhausted. It leaves you thinking about how grief never really goes away, it just changes shape over time.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark comedies and emotional stories about family.
